evidence: src/domain/OrderState.ts defines FULFILMENT_FLOW, nextState and isCancellable; src/domain/Order.ts uses them in advanceTo() and cancel() rather than repeating the transition rules.
src/domain/Product.ts: the stock check exists only in canReserve(quantity); src/domain/StockService.ts reserve() calls product.canReserve(line.quantity) instead of re-implementing it.
src/domain/StockService.ts resolve() and apply() access products only through the ProductRepository interface (findById, save) declared in src/domain/ProductRepository.ts.
src/domain/DomainError.ts DomainErrorKind ('not_found' | 'conflict' | 'invalid') is the error type used in Order.ts, OrderLine.ts, Product.ts and StockService.ts.
src/domain/OrderRepository.ts and src/domain/ProductRepository.ts are ports with matching shapes for the two aggregates (Order, Product).
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain covers one concern, order fulfilment with stock reservation. It has two parts: orders (Order, OrderLine, OrderState, OrderRepository) and stock (Product, ProductRepository, StockService). They share one error type, DomainError. The rule for whether stock is sufficient lives only in Product.canReserve. StockService.reserve calls canReserve on every line before changing anything, so the reserve is all-or-nothing. That is the same rule used twice, not a copy, though both files word similar error messages. The state machine (FULFILMENT_FLOW, nextState, isCancellable) lives only in OrderState.ts, and Order uses those helpers instead of restating the transition logic. StockService loads and saves products only through the ProductRepository interface. All failures use DomainError and its shared kinds. One minor gap: Order.place and Order.mergeLines build OrderLine objects without calling createOrderLine. Merging valid lines can't produce an invalid one, so this falls short of a rubric failure.
